abstract: We give a rigorous, constructive proof that there exists a Ricci-flat K\"ahler metric on the Fermat quartic hypersurface, independently of Yau's famous theorem, along with an explicit and accurate analytic approximation to the metric. The proof combines numerical techniques to obtain the approximately Ricci flat metric, a fixed point theorem to prove existence, and verified numerics to get the bounds used by the fixed point theorem. The method is general and we discuss the computational issues in applying it to other manifolds.
hook: A computer-assisted proof builds a Ricci-flat Calabi-Yau metric on the Fermat quartic from scratch.
summary: Yau proved such metrics exist but never wrote one down. Here numerics produce an approximate metric, and a fixed point theorem with rigorously verified bounds shows a true one lies nearby. It handles one specific surface, the Fermat quartic, though the authors say the method should extend to other manifolds.
title: A constructive computer-assisted existence proof for a Calabi--Yau metric
